flow_tls_encrypted.title: Flow TLS Encrypted
flow_tls_encrypted.description: Attestation: the log/telemetry channel from source to collector/SIEM is wrapped in TLS end-to-end (e.g. syslog-over-TLS on 6514 per RFC 5425, or OTLP with a configured tls block). When false, event bodies — including credentials, PII, and session data — are exposed to any on-path observer and cleartext rewrite becomes trivial.

min_tls_version.title: Minimum TLS Version
min_tls_version.description: Attestation: TLS floor on the log flow. Context for the MITM-modification exposure — a weak floor widens the cert/integrity gap (downgrade-then-rewrite), but is not the load-bearing trigger for any rule here.

server_certificate_validated.title: Server Certificate Validated
server_certificate_validated.description: Attestation: forwarders validate the collector's certificate chain AND hostname end-to-end — no insecure_skip_verify, no insecure: true, no pinning to a self-signed cert without verification. When false, a MITM with any forged or attacker-controlled cert can intercept and rewrite events in transit (RFC 5425 §5 modification threat; OpenTelemetry configtls insecure_skip_verify anti-pattern).

log_pipeline_integrity_protected.title: Log Pipeline Integrity Protected
log_pipeline_integrity_protected.description: Attestation: events crossing this flow carry per-event or per-batch integrity protection (HMAC, signed envelope, hash-chained batch, or equivalent) verified at the SIEM, so an on-path attacker who reaches the wire cannot silently rewrite, drop, or inject records even if TLS is somehow stripped or terminated mid-path. NIST AU-9 requires audit information be protected from unauthorized modification.

service_to_service_mtls_enforced.title: Service-to-Service mTLS Enforced
service_to_service_mtls_enforced.description: Attestation: the log-forwarder-to-collector channel enforces mutual TLS — both peers present and validate X.509 certificates per RFC 5425 §4.2. When false, the collector accepts events from any TLS client (or none), letting an attacker masquerade as a legitimate forwarder and inject fabricated events.

identity_propagated_cryptographically.title: Identity Propagated Cryptographically
identity_propagated_cryptographically.description: Attestation: each emitting workload presents its own cryptographic identity (SPIFFE SVID, per-pod client cert, or unique API key) — not a shared cluster-wide secret. When false, a compromised pod can impersonate any other workload's logs, destroying non-repudiation and enabling spoofed source attribution at the SIEM.

secrets_masked_in_logs.title: Secrets Masked in Logs
secrets_masked_in_logs.description: Attestation: the forwarder/source masks or redacts secrets (API tokens, passwords, JWTs, session identifiers, private-key material) BEFORE events enter the log/telemetry pipeline — not at the central SIEM after exposure. Grounded in CWE-532, OWASP ASVS V7, and the OpenTelemetry redaction processor (allow_all_keys: false with blocked_values regex).

pii_excluded_from_logs.title: PII Excluded from Logs
pii_excluded_from_logs.description: Attestation: personally identifiable information and regulated data (PAN/card numbers, government IDs, full email/phone where not required, health identifiers) are excluded or tokenized at the source before they enter the log pipeline. Grounded in CWE-532, OWASP ASVS V7, PCI DSS Req 3.4/10, and OpenTelemetry redaction processor guidance.

audit_log_tamper_evident.title: Audit Log Tamper Evident
audit_log_tamper_evident.description: Attestation: the log archive / SIEM destination is tamper-evident — WORM, S3 Object Lock (Compliance/Governance), Azure Immutable Blob, GCS Bucket Lock, or append-only indices — so a compromised admin cannot silently delete or rewrite history. NIST AU-9 and MITRE ATT&CK T1070 (Indicator Removal) name this as the primary defensive control.

logging_failure_alerting_enabled.title: Logging Failure Alerting Enabled
logging_failure_alerting_enabled.description: Attestation: a dead-man-switch fires when a source falls silent or the ingest pipeline drops — heartbeat-missing / source-silent-> N min / ingest-rate-collapse rules exist per critical source class with a documented SLO (e.g. page within 15 min). Required by NIST AU-5 and the direct counter to MITRE T1562.006 (Indicator Blocking).

clocks_synced_to_trusted_time_source.title: Clocks Synced to Trusted Time Source
clocks_synced_to_trusted_time_source.description: Attestation: every log source keeps its clock synchronized to a trusted time source (NTP/Chrony, stratum <=4) within bounded skew (e.g. < 1s RMS offset). Per NIST SP 800-92 §4.4 — unsynced clocks let an attacker backdate events to fall outside an evasion window and break cross-source correlation.

timestamps_in_utc.title: Timestamps in UTC
timestamps_in_utc.description: Attestation: all sources emit event timestamps in UTC with sub-second resolution (not local timezone, not a zone-naive wall clock). Per NIST SP 800-92 and OWASP ASVS V7 — non-UTC timestamps break correlation across sources and enable timezone-shift evasion windows.

log_flood_overflow_protection.title: Log Flood Overflow Protection
log_flood_overflow_protection.description: Attestation: the log/telemetry pipeline enforces per-source rate limits AND bounded queues / backpressure (e.g. OpenTelemetry memory_limiter processor, exporterhelper.sending_queue.queue_size, max_recv_msg_size_mib on receivers) so a noisy or compromised source cannot exhaust the SIEM, drop other tenants' signal, or crash the ingest pipeline.
